title: Adler–Fintzen–Mishra–Ohara: refined types and Hecke algebras
body_html:
AFMO Hecke algebra approach

[Adler–Fintzen–Mishra–Ohara] developed a refined type theory and the Heisenberg–Weil datum formalism (an evolution of Yu's generic cuspidal datum that cleanly separates depth-zero from positive-depth parts).

Key items used in this paper:

  • Heisenberg–Weil datum ([AFMO2 §3.6]) — input to Tamely ramified setting: Yu / Kim–Yu / AFMO datum;
  • Twisted Yu representation $\kappa_x$ ([AFMO2 §3.6, p.34 (κ_x defined just above Notation 3.6.4)]) — the representations in [[node:applications.tame_K_F_construction]];
  • Coherence of $\kappa$ under $G$-action ([AFMO2 Prop 3.6.13]) — proves (E2) in [[node:applications.tame_T_axioms]].

Methodological contrast

AFMO's reduction to depth zero goes through explicit Hecke algebra isomorphisms. The present paper supplies a parallel, fully sheaf-theoretic reduction via the §8 Res/Sat functors and the §7.4 localization equivalence. The two routes yield the same equivalence on $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ vs.\ $\Rep_0(M)$ in the tame setting, but the sheaf-side route is more amenable to:

  • handling positive-depth characters uniformly (via the generalized building $\BSigma$);
  • $\ell$-modular generalizations (no Hecke-algebra Bernstein theory needed);
  • bridging to theta correspondence reductions [LM].
